candidate_relations.reason: Epidermolytic hyperkeratosis (EHK) is the umbrella/parent term encompassing the histopathological finding and the broader disease spectrum. AEI is a specific subtype of EHK defined by its annular plaques, milder course, and KRT1 mutations. C001 captures the parent entity but lacks the annular subtype specificity required by the reference diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Epidermolytic hyperkeratosis is the histopathological pattern and broader parent entity; AEI is a distinct clinical subtype characterized by annular morphology and KRT1 mutations

candidate_relations.label: Bullous Congenital Ichthyosiform Erythroderma
candidate_relations.reason: BCIE shares the same histopathological pattern (epidermolytic hyperkeratosis) and can involve KRT1/KRT10 mutations, but it presents with generalized erythroderma and more severe widespread bullae. The clinical record describes annular hyperkeratotic plaques, a milder course with decreasing bullae, and the specific KRT1 c.482T>C variant associated with AEI rather than classic BCIE. Asserting BCIE conflicts with the annular subtype designation.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: BCIE (also called EHK/bullous ichthyosis) is a related but distinct clinical subtype; AEI is differentiated by its annular morphology, milder phenotype, and specific KRT1 variant rather than the generalized erythroderma of BCIE

case_quality_flags: AEI is a rare, well-defined subtype of epidermolytic ichthyosis; KRT1 c.482T>C (p.L161P) and annular morphology are key distinguishing features supporting AEI over classic BCIE or generic EHK
